name: Human blood plasma (example, not reviewed library data)
card:
Example, not reviewed library data. This record is not yet fully human-reviewed and may change in a later commit.

The dynamic viscosity of human blood plasma at 37 °C, 1.33 mPa·s, from Marcinkowska-Gapinska A. and Nawrocka-Bogusz H. (2013), 'Analysis of the Magnetic Field Influence on the Rheological Properties of Healthy Persons Blood', BioMed Research International 2013, article 490410, doi:10.1155/2013/490410 (PMC3775424; CC BY 3.0). The paper tests a magnetic field applied to blood samples; this record holds only the column 'Before magnetic field' of its Table 1, the untreated samples.

The table gives '1.33 ± 0.03' and does not say whether ± is a standard deviation or a standard error, nor which statistic 1.33 is; the paper writes the hematocrit the same way and calls it 'mean value in the group', so 1.33 is recorded as a mean. The ± is recorded in words, its kind unstated.

What the paper states of the donors and the test (section 2, 'Material and Methods'): 25 healthy nonsmoking donors, aged 21 to 51 (mean 31), 19 men and 6 women, free of chronic disease, who passed the standard tests for blood donors; blood in lithium heparin, plasma by centrifugation at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes, measured within 4 hours of collection; a Contraves LS40 rotary-oscillating rheometer, its Couette cell of 1.8 mL used in rotary mode, at 37 °C; viscosity from a regression of shear stress on shear rate over 10 to 100 per second. The paper states that plasma is a Newtonian liquid, citing others. The donor ages are converted to seconds with the Julian year, 31 557 600 s. The record holds no density: the paper reports none.

tissue_state.inferred_from: Material and Methods: 'The interval between the blood collection and the viscosity measurement never exceeded 4 hours.'

preparation.text: Blood collected into BD Vacutainer tubes containing lithium heparin (17 international units/mL of blood); plasma obtained by centrifugation of whole blood at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes and collection of the supernatant; measured within 4 hours of collection.

preservation.reason: Measured within 4 hours of collection; how the samples were kept until then is not stated.

sd.reason: The source gives '1.33 ± 0.03' mPa·s and does not say whether ± is a standard deviation or a standard error. Schema 0.1.0 has no member for a spread of unstated kind.

represents.reason: ± 0.03 mPa·s, of a kind the source does not state.
